item.title: 具身ICL來了創業玩家！上下文成Scaling新賽道
item.abstract: 具身ICL來了創業玩家！上下文成Scaling新賽道 夢晨 2026-09-06 19:44:21 來源： 量子位 讓機器人學會利用更長的多模態Context 衡宇 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 2020年，GPT-3靠“看幾個示例就會新任務”震動了NLP界；六年後的今天，同樣的故事正在具身智慧領域上演。 沒錯，就是 In-Context Learning 。 8月中旬， Skild AI釋出機器人基礎模型S1 。只需要給機器人看一遍任務演示影片，它可以在不微調、不做額外post-training的情況下，嘗試完成此前沒有訓練過的新任務。任務時長可達10分鐘，包含幾十個操作步驟。 Skild在（訓練資料）見過的任務和未見過的任務上，對比了ICL影片Prompt和傳統的語言Prompt VLA。 測試結果表明，當訓練資料只有1000小時時，語言Prompt效果更好，而隨著資料規模增加，ICL開始反超。對於未見任務，加入影片context後，模型表現相比只用語言指令提升約7倍。 S1釋出的一週之前， Generalist AI釋出GEN-1.5，同樣把One-Shot Learning作為核心能力。 機器人只看一個示範，就能在數秒內學習新任務，無需梯度更新或微調，並支援人類示範到機器人執行、組合泛化和Sim-to-Real遷移。 這兩項進展都是在嘗試讓機器人學會利用更長的多模態Context。 In-Context Learning（ICL）這條路徑， 已經在LLM領域被驗證、併成為至關重要的一環。 2020年，OpenAI在GPT-3的論文Language Models are Few‑Shot Learners中提出ICL，定義它是一種能力——不給模型做任何參數更新（沒有微調、反向傳播訓練），僅在輸入prompt中提供若干任務示例（demonstrations/examples），模型在單次前向推理過程中就能夠識別並執行該新任務。 過去三年，上下文從4K擴展到1M，讓模型能一口氣處理一整本書、一個程式碼庫，背後的主要引擎就是ICL。 與LLM不同，具身模型面對的是視覺觀測、語言指令與動作序列交織的複合上下文，且真實任務是非馬爾可夫的——“接下來做什麼”取決於“幾分鐘前做過什麼”。 簡單來說，具身模型面對的上下文是每秒幾十幀視覺觀測，外加本體狀態與動作序列，資訊量高出幾個數量級。 直到今年7月16日，才有李飛飛、Jim Fan、Yuke Zhu等合著的機器人長上下文策略模型與訓練方案 RoboTTT，第一次系統地把“上下文 scaling”這條路線搬到機器人視覺運動策略上。 8月，Generalist和Skild釋出成果。 雖然兩家公司僅以成果釋出形式展示模型效果，技術細節沒有完整公開，但在具身領域，關於ICL討論度隨即驟升。 這條路能否在具身領域真正跑通，取決於一系列遠未解決的技術問題。 也正因為如此，我們產生了更具體的好奇： 如果具身智慧真的要沿著Long Context和ICL繼續往前走，機器人究竟要怎樣理解如此複雜的上下文？ 示範、語言、歷史動作甚至人的糾正，又該怎樣進入模型？ 於是，我們找到了 可可矩陣 （COCO Matrix），一家致力於把In-Context Learning做成具身智慧的底層範式的國內創業公司。 這家公司成立於2026年4月。 不過創始人兼CEO高宇翔告訴我，今年1月深入討論創業相關事宜時，他和自己的co-founder就一致認為是時候著手押注ICL了。 高宇翔 今年30歲，西安交大少年班出身，約翰斯·霍普金斯大學（JHU）博士輟學，在讀期間做人機互動研究。 高宇翔說，GPT-3展現出上下文學習能力時，還在JHU讀博的他就已經在琢磨，這種“不給參數更新、只看示例就會新任務”的能力能不能搬到機器人身上？ 此後五年，他輟學、回國創業、加入工業界、再次創業。 這期間，高宇翔在傅利葉帶隊打通了全尺寸人形機器人從遙操作、資料採集到模型部署的完整鏈路，並在2025年5至8月用一百多萬成本，在全尺寸雙足人形上訓練出具備一定泛化能力的世界模型。 https://about.yuxiang.io/ 今年4月，可可矩陣正式成立，開始把當年在學校裡就開始接觸的問題變成了創業方向。 與Generalist、Skild不一樣，可可矩陣的思路是把後訓練的ICL前置到預訓練階段。 於是，圍繞具身ICL的技術進展、落地難題與行業爭議等，我與高宇翔在上海進行了一場深度對談。 （以下是對話實錄，在不影響本意的前提下略有刪改） 為什麼具身智慧需要換一條Scaling路線？ 量子位 ：過去很長一段時間，具身智慧都沿著大模型的路線Scale資料。大家為什麼相信，堆更多資料就能把機器人能力Scale起來？ 高宇翔 ：最開始整個行業的心態其實都比較樂觀。 早期像ACT、Diffusion Policy這些方案跑通之後，基本解決了behavior cloning、模仿學習的很多核心問題。 當時大家很自然地延續大語言模型的成功邏輯 ，只要持續擴充資料，資料量積累到一定閾值，模型就能湧現出通用能力，最終實現全方位的任務適配。 放在當時的行業環境裡這個思路本身沒有問題，所以整個行業都開始全力規模化擴充資料。 量子位 ：後來問題出在哪裡？ 高宇翔 ：針對單一任務，現在採集兩百條左右的資料，就可以把任務擬合得很好，一個新任務從演示到模型適配，大概十八個小時就能完成。 但 繼續增加資料之後，模型一直沒有出現大家期待的通用泛化能力。 同時，具身資料本身也很難Scale。遙操作資料的質量並不統一，物品和場景多樣性有限，單純依靠這類資料，很難提供足夠豐富的感知覆蓋。 量子位 ：除了這個，還有哪些其它的問題呢？ 高宇翔 ：早期很多VLA沿用了LLM、VLM的預訓練體系，但面向物理世界時，原有視覺表徵很難同時覆蓋機器人需要的不同層級資訊，因此不少方案需要不斷拼接不同的視覺模組。 這套路線在很多場景下依然有效，但過去一年多大家逐漸發現，繼續沿著原有VLA範式疊資料、疊模組，後續能力提升會越來越困難。 具身智慧Scaling路線的新嘗試 量子位 ：如果資料覆蓋走不通，行業現在開始Scale什麼？ 高宇翔 ：能明顯感覺到大家開始關注機器人的學習能力和適應能力。 過去更關注模型在訓練階段見過多少資料、學會多少任務。現在大家開始問另一個問題，機器人到了一個從來沒有見過的新環境、新任務裡，能不能利用當前的Context快速學會。 今年已經出現了一些很明顯的訊號。 像 RoboTTT 這類工作，在嘗試解決更長歷史資訊的編碼、壓縮和利用，讓機器人能夠持續參考更長時間的視覺和動作Context。 Generalist AI、Skild AI最近展示的One-Shot能力更進一步。給機器人看一次任務示範，它就可以基於這段Context快速適配新任務，不需要為每個任務重新做完整的微調或訓練。 所以現在 具身智慧的Scaling維度正在發生擴展 。 除了繼續Scale模型、資料和任務覆蓋之外，機器人在部署之後還能不能繼續學習，能不能從示範、歷史經驗和互動過程中快速獲得新能力，也開始成為一個新的Scaling方向。 LLM驗證過的Scaling邏輯，怎麼到了具身領域這麼難？ 量子位 ：同樣是ICL，具身領域的難度好像比語言模型領域的難度高很多……到底複雜在哪些地方？ 高宇翔 ：機器人面對的是物理世界，它的輸入和任務結構比純語言複雜得多。 這種複雜性主要集中在兩大維度，一是模型本身的輸入輸出與技術架構問題，二是資料體系的先天短板問題。 可以進一步拆成三個核心技術難點。 首先是視覺理解。 機器人在不同任務、不同動作階段，需要的資訊層級並不一樣。它既要理解“這是什麼”這樣的高層語義，也要獲得位置、深度、輪廓等和動作直接相關的精細空間資訊。 這也是早期很多VLA需要同時拼接DINO、CLIP這類不同視覺模型的原因。單一視覺編碼器很難完整覆蓋機器人需要的資訊。 第二是多模態。 語言對機器人來說遠遠不夠。視覺可能承擔大部分資訊，但觸覺、聽覺、本體感知同樣會影響動作。 問題在於這些模態的資料量差異非常大，目前視覺和語言還能依靠海量資料做預訓練對齊，觸覺、聲音和本體狀態的資料規模遠遠沒有達到這個程度。 第三個問題就是Long Context和Memory。 機器人執行的是連續任務，它需要知道之前發生過什麼，還要判斷過去哪些資訊和現在有關。這個過程涉及歷史資訊的壓縮、篩選、提取和長期保留。 實際上，這些支撐機器人長時記憶的基礎技術，也就是最近半年左右才開始出現比較明顯的進展。 從固定視窗到流式記憶 量子位 ：上個月底Skild‑AI的S1模型支援最長10分鐘級別的長任務示範。對比Generalist GEN‑1.5的one‑shot ICL示範影片僅3‑12秒，放在30s視窗內完成現學現用。 雖然Skild給出的是示範demo，但這個時長還是太誇張了。 高宇翔 ：我覺得 不能單純看時長，更重要的是資訊密度 。 如果一段10分鐘的影片裡都是重複動作，沒有新的任務資訊，那它對模型來說並不是高質量Context。 我們現在測試效果比較好的，是人類第一視角或者第三視角的一整段完整任務演示。 人做一遍新任務，機器人看完後，在當前場景裡按照這個任務再完成一次，這種One-Shot Adaptation的資訊密度就很高，因為裡面包含了完整的新任務邏輯、動作和場景資訊。 相反， 如果10分鐘只是很多重複動作，或者是幾個簡單小任務拼起來，它的學習價值反而有限 。 量子位 ：所以Long Context的重點，也不是把固定視窗從一分鐘硬拉到十分鐘？ 高宇翔 ：對。 真實機器人任務裡，很多有效Context可能也就是兩三分鐘。單純讓機器人每次都重新看完整的十分鐘歷史，沒有太大必要。 更重要的是新的Context不斷進入以後，模型能夠持續篩選和壓縮歷史資訊。有些最後保留下來的有效資訊可能來自十分鐘前，也可能來自一小時前。 我們理解的Long Context，更接近一種流式機制 。 最終希望做到機器人可以持續工作、持續利用過去經驗，而不會因為固定Context Window耗盡，一到下午就把早上學到的東西全部忘掉。 量子位 ：但模型本身的視訊記憶體和Context容量畢竟有限，這種長期Memory具體怎麼解決？ 高宇翔 ：目前主要從兩個方向做，這些方案也還在內部測試。 一個是先提升模型自己的理解能力。 模型如果真的理解當前任務，就會更清楚歷史裡哪些資訊重要、哪些資訊可以丟掉。所以Memory並不只是壓縮問題，也和模型理解能力有關。 另一個是對長時序產生的大量KV Cache做壓縮，既要保證即時性，也要控制視訊記憶體消耗。 這方面大語言模型和影片生成已經有不少可以借鑑的技術路線，比如Linear Attention、Sparse Attention，還有基於Routing的關鍵資訊篩選。 我覺得Long Context最後解決的並不是“能塞進去多少東西”，而是有限的模型容量下，能不能一直保留和呼叫真正有用的歷史經驗。 目前ICL還缺什麼樣的資料？ 量子位 ：既然ICL能降低對海量資料的依賴，為什麼資料仍然是一個問題？ 高宇翔 ：ICL降低的主要是對“海量任務全覆蓋資料”的依賴，但基礎資料的數量和多樣性依然很重要。 在UMI這類本體中心資料逐漸普及之前，行業很難獲得以機器人自身動作、本體視角為核心的高質量資料。隨著這類資料越來越多，模型才開始具備比較紮實的基礎操作能力。 ICL並不意味著不再需要資料。 它更像是讓機器人不必為每一個新任務都重新採集大量專項資料，但前提仍然是模型已經建立起足夠好的基礎能力。 量子位 ：那現在最缺的是哪一類資料？ 高宇翔 ：現在比較明顯的缺口，是人機教學、即時糾偏和協同作業這類資料。 如果希望機器人能夠接受人的即時指導，做錯之後被及時糾正，甚至和人一起完成任務，模型就需要見過大量類似的互動過程。 但 目前行業對這類資料還沒有形成成熟的定義和採集體系 。 比如人類手把手教機器人時，哪些資訊需要記錄，糾錯發生在哪個時間點，人的動作、語言和機器人的反饋應該怎麼對齊，這些都還缺少統一標準。 所以我們後續也會重點去定義這類人機教學互動資料，包括應該採什麼、怎麼採，以及怎麼把它用於ICL訓練。 △圖片由AI生成 “強理解，輕生成” 量子位 ：可可矩陣現在在ICL這一塊，整體做到了什麼階段？ 高宇翔 ：整體進度比我原本預期快一些。 量子位 ：你原本的預計是？ 高宇翔 ：一開始我們判斷，光是把模型的理解能力這一塊打磨出來，可能就需要兩三個月。但核心團隊到齊之後，不到一個月，我們已經拿到了足以驗證技術方案可行性的核心證據。 現在這部分技術路線基本已經跑通，下一階段主要是在Scale資料，繼續擴量、精煉資料，把模型能力往上推。 我們現在最核心的判斷是“機器人後面的動作生成能不能做好，很大程度取決於前面到底有沒有把物理世界理解清楚”。 量子位 ：在“理解”這一塊，你們做了什麼不一樣的東西，可以具體聊聊嗎？ 高宇翔 ：我們現在做的是一套“條件表徵”，或者可以理解成條件隱空間。 傳統視覺表徵通常是一幀影像對應一個固定Embedding。無論機器人現在想做什麼，看到這張圖後提取出來的資訊基本是固定的。 但 機器人執行任務不是這樣 。同一張畫面，在不同任務、不同動作階段裡，需要的資訊完全不同。 比如抓一個杯子。剛開始我更關心它是不是杯子，這是語義資訊；真正伸手抓的時候，我更關心它的位置、深度、輪廓和空間關係。 所以 我們認為一個適合機器人的視覺表徵，不應該只由“我看到了什麼”決定，還應該由“我現在想做什麼”共同決定。 我們的模型會根據任務條件和動作意圖，動態提取不同層級的資訊。 現在這套統一模型已經在八、九類視覺任務上做了驗證，包括深度、分割、人體姿態等。 部分任務的能力已經能夠接近上一代專門為單任務訓練的模型，後面主要繼續通過資料把它往當前SOTA推。 量子位 ：是什麼讓你們認定“理解做好以後，動作生成反而可以變輕”？ 高宇翔 ：因為現在很多機器人模型的問題，是前面的表徵裡混進了太多和動作無關的資訊。 比如桌面到底是木紋還是大理石，這對我要不要抓這個杯子基本沒有幫助，但傳統視覺Embedding裡，這些紋理、材質資訊都會一起被編碼進去。 那後面的Action Head就得非常大，自己從一堆混合資訊裡把真正和動作有關的東西篩出來。 我們的思路是在前面的條件表徵階段，就儘量把動作相關資訊提煉出來。 我們做過一個比較極端的實驗。在同樣的訓練設定和算力下，把動作頭壓到大約60M參數，效果依然可以超過一個動作頭達到1.1B左右的對照方案。 所以現在更相信“強理解、輕生成”這個方向。如果前面的視覺理解足夠準確，後面的動作解碼其實沒有必要設計得特別重。 量子位 ：什麼叫“動作相關資訊”？行業裡對這現在有沒有一個統一定義？ 高宇翔 ：目前還沒有特別統一、讓我覺得足夠完善的（定義）。 現在行業裡比較常見的一條路線是Latent Action Model。 很多人類影片、生成影片，本身沒有機器人動作標註，所以大家會訓練一個隱變數，去表示幀與幀之間發生了什麼變化，把它當成一種“替代動作”。 常見做法有兩類。 一種是只要從第一幀能夠推到第二幀，就認為中間的變化包含動作資訊；另一種是通過光流，把畫素在空間裡的變化作為動作表徵。但這些方案都有問題。 比如光流很稠密，但很難區分到底是相機在動，還是機器人、人物本身在動。人體關鍵點相對更穩定，不太受相機運動影響，但它的資訊又比較稀疏。 所以我們沒有先人為規定一個非常嚴格的“動作表示”應該是什麼。 現在會把人類手部關鍵點、全身關鍵點、光流等多種和動作相關的預測任務放進同一個條件表徵模型裡訓練，讓不同資訊彼此補充。 後面如果發現新的預測任務能夠幫助動作生成，也可以繼續加入訓練。 我們 更希望模型能力的提升來自資料和訓練任務本身，而不是不斷在結構上做複雜修改。 成功率之外，怎麼衡量機器人的學習能力？ 量子位 ：現在可可基礎模型的One-Shot能力，大概做到什麼水平？ 高宇翔 ：目前比較明確的是簡單任務。比如常規抓取類任務，在臨時改變目標、做One-Shot Adaptation之後，完成率可以穩定在80%以上。 我們現在 不僅僅是單獨看One-Shot成功率，還要看它和專項Post-training後的能力差距有多大。 理想狀態下，機器人只看一次示範、在Context裡完成快速適配之後，效果應該儘可能接近針對這個任務專門訓練出來的模型。 複雜任務目前還沒有完整評測，因為對應模型還在繼續訓練。 量子位 ：主攻One-Shot的同時，為什麼還去做Self-Correction？ 高宇翔 ：因為人類學習新任務也不是看一遍之後，每次都能第一次成功。 但失敗以後，你會知道哪裡出了問題，下次會針對性調整。我們希望機器人也有這種能力。 第一次執行失敗之後，模型會重新利用這段失敗軌跡，判斷哪裡需要修正，再進行下一次嘗試。 △圖片由AI生成 所以Self-Correction其實也是In-Context Learning的一種形態。Context不只來自別人給出的示範，也可以來自機器人自己剛剛經歷過的失敗。 我們的目標是即使第一次沒有完成任務，機器人也能通過後續幾次自主嘗試和糾正，最終完成任務。 量子位 ：假如——我是說假如——如果機器人可以不斷試錯，那以後“成功率”是不是也不夠用了？ 高宇翔 ：對，所以我們之後可能會更關注另外一個指標——第一次成功平均耗時。 如果機器人能夠持續嘗試、持續Self-Correction，那麼單純問“一次任務成功率是多少”，意義會越來越有限。 更有價值的問題是，它看完一次示範之後，要花多久才能第一次把這個任務學會。 這個時間其實對應的就是機器人的教學成本和學習效率。 對於抓取這種簡單任務，我們希望它看一次就能第一次成功。 但像疊衣服，甚至把衣服疊成大象、天鵝這種，人類自己可能也需要幾個小時學習。那我們希望機器人的學習週期，至少可以逐漸接近正常人的培訓週期。 如果這套能力成立，一個地方、一臺機器人學會的新技能，後面也可以被其他機器人繼續複用。 所以以後衡量機器人智慧，可能不只是看它已經會多少任務，還要看它學會一個新任務到底需要多久。 為什麼要自己創業？ 量子位 ：你本科就從自駕轉向了機器人，大概是十年前。 高宇翔 ：對，我本科在西安交大少年班，最開始做自動駕駛，大概2016年前後開始轉向機器人。 那個時候我就覺得，機器人這個問題比自動駕駛更複雜，它同時涉及硬體、演算法和資料，而且要解決的場景更多樣。 後來從JHU博士生輟學，我來了工業界，尤其是人形機器人、資料和模型落地這一側。 量子位 ：我看你是從機器人公司傅利葉出來創業的。 高宇翔 ：對的。我2024年的時候加入了傅利葉。 這幾年我較早參與打通了全尺寸人形機器人的遙操作、資料採集到模型部署這一整套流程，也參與了一些大規模VLA訓練。

item.title: OKF Agent Memory – Git-native persistent memory for AI coding agents
item.abstract:
OKF Agent Memory A Domain-Neutral, Git-Native Persistent Project Memory for AI Agents based on the Open Knowledge Format (OKF) v0.2. 🌟 Overview Conversations with AI agents reset when context windows close. Valuable architectural decisions, domain discoveries, and operational facts are lost unless stored persistently. OKF Agent Memory provides a standardized, vendor-neutral memory layer that lives directly in your repository ( knowledge/ ) as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. It bridges the gap between unstructured ad-hoc markdown files ( CLAUDE.md , AGENTS.md ) and complex, black-box vector databases. flowchart TD L1["1. OKF v0.2 Specification
(Normative Markdown & YAML Format)"] L2["2. Agent Memory Convention
(Behavioral Rules: Search, Review, Trust)"] L3["3. Agent Skill
(LLM Prompts & Operational Workflows)"] L4["4. Tooling Layer: Go Library & CLI
(Deterministic Parsing, Validation, Search, MCP)"] L5["5. Project Knowledge Corpus
(knowledge/ OKF Bundle)"] L1 --> L2 L2 --> L3 L3 --> L4 L4 --> L5 Loading ⚡ Key Highlights Blazing Fast Performance (<300µs Search, ~4ms Graph Validation) : In-memory BM25 retrieval and bundle validation execute in microseconds without VM spin-up or network roundtrips. 100% Git-Native & Zero Vendor Lock-in : Everything is version-controlled plain text. Inspect, audit, and review your agent's memory using standard git diff and git log . No external database required. Zero API Costs for Memory Retrieval : Local lexical BM25 indexing eliminates recurring vector embedding API costs and network roundtrips. Built on Google OKF v0.2 : Uses the open standard format for agent knowledge with full support for provenance ( sources ), trust tiers ( generated vs. verified ), and lifecycle metadata ( status , stale_after ). Solves Context Bloat & Memory Rot : Employs Progressive Disclosure (hierarchical index.md files and link graphs) so agents only load the exact concepts they need. Search-Before-Write Principle : Mandates querying existing memory before authoring, preventing concept duplication and hallucinated divergence. Zero-Dependency Go Toolchain : Single binary with zero external dependencies , sub-5ms CLI startup time, and a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server ( okf mcp ). Truly Domain-Neutral : Designed for Software Engineering, Coaching, Scientific Research, Literature Reviews, and Operations. 📊 Performance Benchmarks Built in Go with zero external dependencies, okf is engineered for high-frequency agent tool calling loops: Benchmark Metric Python / Vector DB Runtimes (Mem0, Letta) Deno / Node.js Tooling OKF Agent Memory (Go) Concept Search Latency 150ms – 800ms (Embedding API + Vector DB) 40ms – 120ms < 300 µs (Microseconds, In-Memory BM25) Full Corpus Parse & Graph Validation 200ms – 1.5s 80ms – 250ms ~4.0 ms (50+ concepts, bidirectional graph) Process Cold-Start Overhead 250ms – 600ms (Python VM boot) 80ms – 180ms (V8 / Deno boot) < 4 ms (Compiled Single Binary) Retrieval Cost per 1,000 Queries ~$0.10 – $0.50 (Embedding tokens) $0.00 $0.00 (Zero API cost, fully local) Memory Footprint (RSS) ~120 MB – 350 MB ~60 MB – 140 MB < 15 MB Tip Reproduce Locally with your own LLM : We provide an automated benchmark runner in pure Go to verify Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) speedups and -80% token reduction on your local hardware (LM Studio / Ollama with Gemma, Qwen, Llama). Run make benchmark or explore the Progressive Disclosure Benchmark Suite . 🚀 Quickstart 1. Build the Tooling Clone the repository and compile the standalone okf executable: make build This generates the standalone binary at bin/okf . 2. Basic CLI Commands # Validate bundle conformance, graph connectivity, and description drift ./bin/okf validate knowledge --strict --drift # Search concepts via in-memory BM25 scoring ./bin/okf search " architecture layers " knowledge # Inspect a concept and its relationships (with --json support) ./bin/okf show architecture/layers knowledge --json # Create a new concept with automated log.md and index.md bookkeeping ./bin/okf create decisions/auth-flow knowledge \ --type Decision \ --title " OAuth2 Authorization Flow " \ --desc " Standardized on PKCE for client authentication. " # Update an existing concept ./bin/okf update decisions/auth-flow knowledge \ --desc " Updated OAuth2 PKCE token refresh interval. " # Bootstrap full agent memory stack into any target project ./bin/okf bootstrap /path/to/project --name " My Project " # Initialize only a bare OKF bundle in any directory ./bin/okf init my-project/knowledge 3. Bootstrapping Agent Memory in Any Project Scaffold the complete OKF Agent Memory architecture into any new or existing repository with a single command: # Bootstrap full memory stack into target project ./bin/okf bootstrap /path/to/my-project --name " My Service " This automatically sets up: knowledge/ — OKF v0.2 compliant persistent memory bundle ( index.md , log.md ) .agents/skills/okf-memory/ — Embedded agent skill definition and capability guides AGENTS.md — Project-tailored operating instructions for AI coding agents Makefile — Convenience tasks for validation ( make validate ) and search ( make search q="..." ) 4. Running as an MCP Server okf ships with a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over stdio to seamlessly connect with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other agent platforms: ./bin/okf mcp knowledge Example MCP Configuration ( claude_desktop_config.json or Cursor): { "mcpServers" : { "okf-memory" : { "command" : " /path/to/okf-agent-memory/bin/okf " , "args" : [ " mcp " , " /path/to/project/knowledge " ] } } } 📂 Repository Structure okf-agent-memory/ ├── benchmarks/ # item.title: LLMs as a Cognitive Virus
item.abstract:
Physics > Physics and Society [Submitted on 3 Sep 2026] Title: Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus Authors: Ricard Solé , Giulio Ruffini , Francesca Castaldo , Marco Tuccio , Luis F. Seoane , Manlio de Domenico , Santiago F. Elena , David C. Krakauer , Michael Levin View a PDF of the paper titled Large-Language Models as a Cognitive Virus, by Ricard Sol\'e and 8 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Large-language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming part of human culture, reshaping how information is produced, transmitted, and used. Here we propose that their diffusion can be understood through a viral analogy, with LLM use spreading through populations, becoming embedded in cognitive and cultural practices. We model transitions among uncoupled, coupled, and persistently dependent users, and show that the interplay between social transmission, recovery, and collective reinforcement can generate tipping points and technological lock-in. A central consequence is the possibility of runaway dynamics: once a critical threshold is crossed, small increases in adoption can trigger rapid population-level shifts toward persistent dependence, with abrupt losses in cognitive competence. The same framework, however, identifies conditions for cognitive immunization, based on reducing transmission and facilitating reversibility. Our results highlight how LLM adoption may involve nonlinear collective transitions with important consequences for cognitive autonomy. item.title: Claude Mythos 5.1 and Fable 5.1: Capabilities
item.abstract: This is the weirdest situation in which to write a capabilities review. Introducing the world’s most powerful model, by a substantial margin. No wait, this just in, we also have someone else introducing the world’s most powerful model. Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra are both excellent models. This much, we know. Fable 5.1 comes with reduced cache prices, the option of zero data retention and substantially more lenient classifiers than Fable 5. Early signs are, with large error bars, that the jump from Sol to Astra is bigger and more exciting than the jump from Fable 5 to Fable 5.1. This may be similar to how the scaling move from Opus to Fable was a big deal. With the exception of token use, Fable 5.1 got almost universally positive feedback in absolute terms. Reports are that Fable 5.1 is highly well-rounded. Writing is greatly improved. The Claudisms seem to have improved, although some are very much still there. It admits mistakes. People enjoy their conversations. Several people noted it simplifies code. The safety classifiers are less obnoxious. Fable 5.1 loves being proactive and doing all the things. If you give it a high effort level, it will find things to do with those tokens. Often they will be useful things. My own experience has been that Fable 5.1 and Astra are both excellent. In the one case I’ve had the chance to compare responses on a hard question, both answers were different and very good, complementing each other. My plan is to ‘dual wield’ and ask both all non-trivial queries, at least for a while. Mostly this review of necessity looks at Fable 5.1 in isolation, rather than being able to compare it to Astra, and most of those who react are doing likewise. There will be full coverage of Astra in turn, which will give more opportunity for comparisons. As usual, Anthropic basically said ‘here is the new model with the higher number.’ The coding department thinks it is very good at coding, also Our Price Cheap. Boris Cherny (Claude Code Creator, Anthropic): Fable 5.1 is our best model yet for coding, data analysis, computer use, design, presentations, Tag, and the hardest long-running agentic work. This model is a pleasure to work with, and I’ve been using it for everything. We have also reduced prices for Enterprise, API, and SDK customers. Cache reads on Fable 5.1 are now $0.25 per million tokens (previously: $1). Up to 38% cheaper for a typical Claude Code session. We have been working on how often safeguards intervene. Our latest biology safeguards intervene on benign requests 85% less often than the ones we shipped with Fable 5, and Claude Code users should see around 60% fewer cyber interventions per session. Expect more improvements soon. Last but not least, Fable 5.1 writes better and has better tone. We heard your feedback, and are actively working on reducing Claude-speak. Solid progress with 5.1, more to come. Alex Albert highlights its ability to generate videos through code. His example is he took a picture of a property lot, and told Fable to design a house, render it, and produce a cinematic walkthrough, short video at link . They spend a section on scientific research. That’s also an OpenAI point of emphasis. Anthropic is doing a strange thing with Fable 5.1 pricing. The headline price is unchanged from Fable 5, but the effective price is lower because they are reducing the pricing on cache reads from $1 to $0.25 per million tokens. This will lower typical per-token costs by 25% and highly agentic work costs by ‘up to approximately 45%,’ consistent with Boris’s 38% cheaper for typical Claude Code use: I presume this aligns incentives, by lining up with actual costs, but I would have been inclined to put some of the discount in headline costs instead. People are simple creatures, you have to talk to them on their level sometimes. LLM Index : Claude Fable 5.1 is live on OpenRouter. Anthropic’s new model arrives at $10.00/M input, $50.00/M output. No predecessor price or history hook attached. The clean read is the listing itself: a premium Claude shelf entry, now priced on OpenRouter. Fable 5 never got above about 11% of Anthropic dollar spend on Ramp, despite being the clearly best model out there. Two of the big objections were the safeguards having a large blast radius that stopped ordinary work, and companies, often due to various regulatory concerns, failing to abide Anthropic’s data retention policy, where they required records be kept for 30 days. The individual Dude , who could abide, had huge coding edge. Anthropic has heard you, and had some time to get more comfortable, and for the government to calm down versus when it was so nervous it forced Fable offline over a supposed ‘jailbreak.’ Anthropic is working on a new system that will allow ‘eligible customers’ to use Fable 5.1 with zero outside data retention, via letting the customer store the data. Until then, full zero data retention is available for those customers. They’ve greatly reduced the false positive rate on the classifiers (at least 60%). That is too many changes at once, including model improvements and lower prices, but will be a fascinating natural experiment. We should see massive adoption of Fable 5.1 within the Anthropic ecosystem, far more than the 11% for Fable 5. If we do not, then people really are purely balking at the headline price without thinking that through. Anthropic shares a ton of benchmarks. Mostly we see modest improvement from Fable 5 or Opus 5 to Fable 5.1, with some small regressions. I’m listing them so you can get a quick gestalt. There does not seem to be a clear pattern. Fable 5.1 came out prior to GPT-6, so here is where things stood at that time. All ‘slash line’ scores I give, e.g. 50%/70%, refer to scores without and then with tools. All improvement or regression numbers by default are versus the best score of either Opus 5 or Mythos 5. All numbers are rounded to the given significant figures, as per my judgment. Life sciences evals overall show modest improvement and are covered in post one. Parenthesis on Terminal Bench 4.0 is for Mythos, other scores are for Fable. I have added Astra to the chart, based on what we could find. The Anthropic ECI score is 162.0, versus 159.5 for Mythos 5 and 160.7 for Opus 5, exactly on the Mythos-era trend line. DeepSWE v1.1 score was 67.4% over 5 trials, but with no frame of reference. FrontierCode 1.1 Extended scores are worse at higher effort levels. Anthropic attributes that to Fable 5.1 being unable to stop itself from making additional helpful edits at higher effort levels, which get it marked as incorrect. FrontierSWE v2 score was 0.57 versus 0.52 for Opus 5, 0.48 for Fable 5 and 0.32 for Sol. Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 was a big jump to 52.6% from 24.7%. CursorBench 3.2 maxed out at 73.4% versus a max out of 70.5% for Fable 5, at a substantially lower total cost. Sol maxes out at 67.2%. CritPT-Corrected slightly improved from 85.5% to 88.4%. ArXivMath slightly improved from 91%/91% to 91%/94%. ProgramBench improved slightly from 86.3% to 87.6%. As per the chart, Humanity’s Last Exam improved from 57.8%/63.8% to 60.9%/65%. They run various multi-agent tests, but don’t provide good points of comparison, so I can’t tell how good the results are. Chartography improved from 37%/84% to 43%/86%. BenchCAD Vision2Code improved from 38%/67% to 44%/84%. OSWorld 2.0 improves as per the chart from 75% partial, 39% strict to 78% partial and 42% strict. Anthropic’s more lenient version of GDP.pdf does not clearly improve. Without tools improves from 83% to 85%, but Fable 5 retains the high score with tools at 87% versus 85% for Fable 5.1. It is strange that Fable 5.1 got no help from tools but that is what was reported. OfficeQA score was 80%, OfficeQA Pro was 69%, versus previous Claude highs of 79% and 67%. Legal Agent Benchmark from Harvey AI scored a 19.1% all-pass rate and 90.8% mean criterion-pass under max effort, or on the held out set 16.7% and 93.3%.

item.title: 🗞️ByteDance's $30B Loan, Moonshot's IPO Filing, and China's Hottest AI Chip Debut Yet
item.abstract: China AI Weekly Digest summarizes the week’s big news, model updates, policy, products, and research, sourced from the aggregated newsfeed of China AI Index . The digest below is mostly compiled and drafted by an AI agent sourcing from credible news outlets, then fact-checked and edited by me. This week: 231 stories tracked (74 English-language, 157 Chinese-language 🇨🇳) over 2026-08-29–2026-09-05. ByteDance has secured a loan worth roughly $30 billion to fund its AI buildout. The facility ranks as Asia’s second-largest loan of the year, according to Bloomberg. Meanwhile ByteDance is reportely expanding a massive AI data-centre cluster in Inner Mongolia, signaling that the compute race in China is now being financed less through equity than through sheer balance-sheet leverage. ( Reuters / Bloomberg / The Information ) Moonshot AI has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO, targeting a listing as early as the first quarter of 2027. A final pre-IPO round could value the company at roughly $50 billion. Kimi K3, released in July, became the largest open-weight model on the market at more than 2.8 trillion parameters and drew real attention in Silicon Valley for catching up US proprietary models at lower prices. Moonshot itself declined to comment on “market rumours or speculation.” ( Reuters / SCMP / The Information ) Enflame’s Shanghai IPO closed out a historic fundraising wave for China’s AI chip “little dragons.” The chipmaker priced 43 million shares at ¥142.18 each to raise about $910 million, and retail demand hit as high as 6,109 times subscription, an eye-popping number even by STAR Market average. Enflame is one of the four domsetic chip upstarts to complete a mega-raise this year, after Moore Threads ($8 billion), MetaX ($4.2 billion), and Biren ($897 million). Unlike those rivals, it’s betting on domain-specific chip architecture over general-purpose GPUs, and it will need that raise to wean itself off heavy revenue dependence on backer Tencent. ( SCMP / Reuters / Bloomberg ) Tencent’s frontier model made the week’s biggest jump, and China’s agent platforms kept multiplying. Tencent’s Hy4 preview leapt from 34th to 8th place on the Code Arena WebDev leaderboard and outperformed other top open models on the DeepSWE coding benchmark. Goldman Sachs analysts credit a “closed-loop” strategy—shipping preview models into Tencent’s own products first, then feeding real user interactions back into training—as the edge behind the gain. ( SCMP / SCMP ) Alibaba’s Qwen team pushed a Qwen3.8-Max-0902 refresh, 2.4 trillion parameters, a 1M-token context window, and further post-training on coding and enterprise “cowork” tasks. ( @Alibaba_Qwen ) Ant Group open-sourced two vertical Ling-3.0-flash models this week: Sante, tuned for medical reasoning and healthcare tasks, and Fin, a finance-focused release paired with FinFIRST, a new benchmark for financial search agents. ( @AntLingAGI / @AntLingAGI ) MiniMax’s model is powering Saudi Arabia’s Humain in a new Arabic-language model, the kind of Gulf-market foothold Chinese labs have been chasing all year. ( Bloomberg / The Information ) The enterprise-agent land grab continued: Tencent opened its WorkBuddy agent platform with more than 100 launch partners, and Alibaba Cloud put its own enterprise agent-collaboration platform, Wanyou Wujie (萬有無界), into public beta. ( 雷峰網 / 雷峰網 ) IPO fever wasn’t limited to the Big Three. The pipeline behind it is just as busy. China’s AI “little giant” Yunxi Technology has filed for a Hong Kong IPO, per sources cited by SCMP. ( SCMP ) Momenta and Horizon Robotics, two of the top public ADAS technology supplies, edge toward breakeven, according to their first half-year report. ( 36Kr ) China’s No. 2 foundry Hua Hong is putting $2 billion into a new fab to meet surging AI-driven chip demand. ( SCMP ) First-half results split China’s AI chipmakers into clear winners and laggards: MetaX swung to a ¥612 million profit on 44.7% revenue growth and Biren shares jumped 18.8% in Hong Kong trading, while Iluvatar Corex slid 2.2% on investor concern over weaker performance. ( SCMP ) Z.ai (Zhipu) posted 400% first-half revenue growth with narrowing losses, even as a separate Bloomberg report said the lab’s sales still missed estimates as China’s AI price war weighs on margins. ( SCMP / Reuters ) Global investors are descending on Shenzhen to chase AI and robotics opportunities. ( SCMP ) The dominant thread this week was the looming Trump-Xi summit on AI safety. Washington and Beijing are gearing up for AI safety talks in mid-September as both sides lay groundwork for a Trump-Xi summit; separately, Beijing rebuked Anthropic and set its own terms for the dialogue, while an OpenAI executive publicly urged the two governments to prioritize safety talks. ( Reuters / Bloomberg / SCMP ) Separately, a bill advanced in the US Congress aims to give America an edge in the open-source AI race with China. item.title: Chrome again exempts Google from user site data settings
item.abstract:
Six years ago I published a blog post Chrome exempts Google sites from user site data settings that received quite a bit of attention: Michael Tsai , Hacker News The Register , The Verge , and Gizmodo , among others. The blog post was about a Google Chrome bug that mysteriously exempted Google-owned sites from the setting to automatically delete all site data. Eventually, spurred by my report, Google did fix the bug. You can probably guess why I’m writing about the bug again: I’ve noticed Chrome doing something similar now. I’ve reproduced this new issue on two different Macs with Chrome version 152.0.7977.83. For testing purposes, I changed the default search engine in Chrome from Google to DuckDuckGo, just to make sure that this setting was not the cause. On-device site data settings ( chrome://settings/content/siteData ) shows that the Default behavior is to Delete data sites have saved to your device when you close all windows. I’m not signed into Chrome and indeed disallow Chrome sign-in. You can see on chrome://settings/content/all that no site data is saved. Then I close the one and only window in Chrome. Returning to chrome://settings/content/all , I find some google.com site data! This data persists even if I quit and relaunch Chrome. If I delete the Google site data and repeat the whole process, the same issue occurs again. As far as I can tell, www.google.com is the only site exempted by Chrome. Looking inside the ~/Library /Application Support /Google /Chrome /Default folder, it appears that the saved site data consists of Cookies, Local Storage, and Session Storage. I’m not certain when this issue was introduced. My default web browser is Safari, so I don’t use Chrome full-time, though I do use it (and Firefox) frequently for testing. I’m personally inclined to cite Hanlon’s razor here rather than engage in conspiracy theories. Nonetheless, Google has no excuse for incompetence either, especially given the amount of money made by the company (which I’ll always call Google, not Alphabet) and its engineers. They can avoid receiving bad publicity from me by improving their QA. Perhaps some kind of unit tests for this feature? Move slower and don’t break things. I wish the government would move fast and break up the Google Search monopoly. Don’t even get me started about how when you’re not signed in to Google, all Google Search results are now opaque https://www.google.com/goto?url= garbage rather than the site URLs!

item.title: You Don't Have a Right to Safe Drinking Water, US Court Rules
item.abstract:
A volunteer grabs a gallon of water at a water and food distribution drive held by College Hill Baptist Church and the World Central kitchen on March 7, 2021 in Jackson, Mississippi. Michael M. Santiago/Getty Get your news from a source that’s not owned and controlled by oligarchs. Sign up for the free Mother Jones Daily . On Friday, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of a lawsuit against the city of Jackson, Mississippi, which alleged the city knowingly let residents drink lead-contaminated water. The lawsuit, first filed in 2022 , says the contamination violated Jacksonians’ constitutional right to bodily integrity. Donald Trump-appointed judge Kurt Engelhardt disagreed . “The Constitution does not provide redress for every governmental wrongdoing,” Engelhardt said. “Defendants’ actions allegedly deprived Plaintiffs of clean water and guileless information. These deprivations, while grievous, do not infringe upon any deeply rooted constitutional right.” That may be true in Mississippi—but on the state level in at least nine US states, and in more than a dozen other countries, clean drinking water is in fact a protected right. In countries including Uruguay and South Africa , a right to clean water is enshrined in the constitution. New York’s state constitution, as of a 2021 amendment , states that “each person shall have a right to clean air and water, and a healthful environment.” So too in Massachusetts, where “the right to clean air and water” has been constitutionally protected since 1972 . But according to the Fifth Circuit ruling, the US constitution is too narrow for such a claim. The Jackson plaintiffs alleged that their city government deliberately withheld information about the water’s toxicity, and exacerbated the problem through a series of boil-water notices—a practice that can eliminate some bacterial contamination, but also concentrates lead in water. Engelhardt stated there is no “constitutional right to truthful information from officials during a public health crisis.” Jackson is more than 80 percent Black and has a poverty rate that is more than double the national average. The city’s water system has long been in dire need of upgrades . In 2015, officials from the Mississippi State Department of Health found elevated lead levels in the water supply. Instead of immediately informing citizens, they remained silent about the issue for six months , according to reporting from Grist , while residents continued drinking toxic water. EPA officials ran a series of tests in 2020 and found “persistent and concerning violations” of water safety policy, including leaks, corrosion, and high lead levels throughout the system. But no city, state, or federal agencies fixed the problem. Meanwhile, people including Jackson plaintiff Priscilla Sterling continued drinking water with unsafe levels of lead. According to the 2022 lawsuit, several of Sterling’s children have since been diagnosed with lead poisoning, which can cause permanent brain damage. A quarter of Jackson’s residents are children, who are particularly vulnerable to the life-long effects of lead poisoning . The Fifth Circuit ruling comes as the Trump administration moves to weaken clean-water-related protections. Also on Friday, Trump’s EPA released a supplemental rule to further dilute the Clean Water Act, quickly condemned by environmental watchdogs. “The administration is clearly struggling to craft a rule that will hold up in court while satisfying their donors’ desire to effectively scrap these protections wherever possible,” said Jim Murphy of the National Wildlife Federation. “One thing is clear: If we don’t protect our streams and wetlands, the cost of dirtier drinking water and increased flooding will flow downstream to households at a time when most Americans are living paycheck to paycheck.”
